لكا: لَكَأَ 1 , aor. ﹷ, (K,) inf. n. لَكْءٌ, (TA,) He beat a person (K) with a whip. (TA.) === لَكَأَ بِهِ الأَرْضَ He cast him upon the ground. (AZ, S.) [See زَكَأَ, and لَتَأَ.] === لَكَأَهُ He prostrated him. (K.) ___ لَكَأَهُ He gave him the whole of what was due to him: (K:) like لَفَأَهُ. (T.) ___ لَكِئَ, aor. ﹷ, He stayed, dwelt, or abode, (K,) in a place: like لَكِىَ. (TA.) لكئ بِمَوْضِعٍ He kept, or remained fixed, in a place. (K, * TA.)
لكث: لَكَثَ 1 , [aor. ﹹ,] inf. n. لَكْثٌ (and لِكَاثٌ, IAar), He struck, or smote; (K;) accord. to IAar, who does not particularize the hand, nor the foot: (TA:) or, with his hand, or his foot, accord. to some: (TA:) or, with [perhaps a mistake for upon] the mouth. (Kr.) [See also لكد.] === لَكَتَهُ, [aor. ﹹ,] He overburdened him. (K.) === لَكِثَ, aor. ﹷ, [inf. n. لَكَثٌ,] He (a camel) was affected with the disorder called لَكَثٌ, or لُكَاثٌ. (K.) === لَكِثَ بِهِ, aor. ﹷ, It (dirt [see لَكْثٌ]) adhered to it; (K;) i. e., to the vessel. (TA.) [See also لَكِدَ and لَكِعَ.]
لَكْثٌ The dirt of milk, which congeals upon the edge of the vessel, and is removed with the hand. (TA.)

لَكَثٌ and 🡻لُكَاثٌ (as also نُكَاثٌ, TA,) A disorder in the mouths of camels, resembling pustules. (Lh, K.) === 🡻لُكَاثَةٌ, A disorder that attacks sheep or goats in the sides of the mouth and in the lips, resembling an ulcer; happening on their first cropping plants when they are short, with small branches. (L.)
لكاث: لُكَاثٌ A shining stone in gypsum. (Fr, K.) ___ See لَكَثٌ.
لُكَّاثٌ [pl. of لَاكِثٌ?] Preparers of gypsum: (K:) not those who traffick therein. (TA.)
لكاثي: لُكَاثِىٌّ A man (TA) very white: (K:) from لُكَاثٌ as signifying a shining stone in gypsum. (TA.)
لكزه: لَكَزَهُ 1 , aor. ﹹ, (Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. لَكْزٌ, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He struck him upon the breast (AO, S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) with the fist: (AO, S, Mgh, Msb:) and upon the حَنَك [or part beneath the chin]: (A, K:) and upon the neck: (K:) or upon any part of the body with the fist: (AZ, S, Msb:) or with the extremities of the fingers: (TA, art. لقز:) he pushed, or impelled, or repelled, him: (TA, ibid.:) he thrust or pierced him [with a spear or the like]: (TA, art. لز:) لَكْزٌ is also syn. with وَكْزٌ [which has several significations, some of which are indentical with some explained above]. (K.) You say also, لَكَزَهُ بِجُمْعِ كَفِّهِ He struck him upon the breast, or the part called حَنَك, with his fist. (A.)
لكزة: لَكْزَةٌ A blow upon the breast, (A, Mgh,) and upon the part beneath the chin, [&c.,] (A,) with the fist. (Mgh.)
لكه: لكَّهُ 1 He pushed him, or thrust him; like دَكَّهُ and صَكَّهُ. (As, TA in art. دك.)
لكاك: لِكَاكٌ A pressing, or crowding: see an ex. voce عَكَّهٌ.
لكز: لَكْزٌ [inf. n. of لَكَزَهُ] i. q. طَعْنٌ, like لَزٌّ. (TA, art. لز.)
لكمه: لَكْمَهٌ A blow with the fist.
لكنة: لُكْنَةٌ An impotence, or impediment, or a difficulty, in speech or utterance; (Msb;) a barbarousness, or viciousness, and an impotence, or impediment, in speech: (S:) or the not speaking Arabic rightly, by reason of a barbarousness, or viciousness, in the tongue: (K:) or the interposing of [words of] a foreign language in one's speech. (Mbr, TA.) See تَهْتَهَةٌ; and عُجْمَةٌ, with which it is syn.
لكن: لٰكِنْ , with the ن quiescent, has no government. === It means But after a negative proposition: but not after an affirmative: see إِلَّا.
